title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors and employees
tiers.description: All Directors and employees of K&S; bound by the general insider trading prohibition on buying, selling or otherwise dealing in K&S Securities while in possession of inside information.

tiers.name: Directors and Senior Executives
tiers.description: Directors and Senior Executives of K&S; subject to the 60-day Black Out Periods before half-year and full-year results, Excluded Trading carve-outs, and Chairman/Deputy Chairman clearance for exceptional-circumstances trading in a Black Out Period.

tiers.name: Directors, Secretary and Senior Executives
tiers.description: Directors, the Company Secretary and Senior Executives; distinguished only for the margin loan/secured finance notification and ASX disclosure regime in section 11.

tiers.name: Family members
tiers.description: Referenced informally (a family member, friend, family company or trust) as persons who must not be advised, procured or encouraged to deal while the Director or employee holds inside information; not separately defined as a formal 'Associate' term.

windows.start_anchor: 60 days prior to the release of K&S's half year financial results to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: release of K&S's half year financial results to the ASX

windows.start_anchor: 60 days prior to the release of K&S's full year financial results to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: release of K&S's full year financial results to the ASX

rules.detail: 'K&S Securities' is defined only as shares in K&S Corporation Limited; the policy nowhere mentions options, derivatives, warrants or other financial products, so an OTC put/call (particularly if cash-settled) is not itself a dealing in K&S Securities and falls outside the Black Out Period, clearance and insider trading provisions on their literal wording.
Hedging, and unvested equity incentive securities, are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Monetisation is not named and there is no agreement-to-deal catch-all; a prepaid forward or similar structure is not addressed.
Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named; given 'K&S Securities' means shares only, a cash-settled CFD would not obviously be caught.

Margin lending is not prohibited or subject to prior approval; the person must advise the Company Secretary, who informs all other Directors, and the Company Secretary discloses to the ASX only where security interests or third-party rights reach 5% of issued K&S shares, without disclosing trigger-price detail.
rules.evidence: Where the holding of a Director, Secretary or Senior Executive of K&S Securities has been financed via a margin loan or other secured finance arrangement (eg, mortgage, charge or lien ... ), the Company Secretary must be advised and the Company Secretary will inform all other Directors.

rules.detail: A mortgage, charge or lien over K&S Securities (any 'other secured finance arrangement') is expressly named and treated the same as a margin loan: notify the Company Secretary, with ASX disclosure only at the 5% threshold.
rules.evidence: financed via a margin loan or other secured finance arrangement (eg, mortgage, charge or lien (other than a loan from K&S under the K&S Employee Share Plan))

rules.detail: The provision is not limited to margin loans; 'other secured finance arrangement' expressly covers any secured financing of the holding, subject only to notifying the Company Secretary and, above a 5% security-interest threshold, ASX disclosure (excluding trigger-price detail).
rules.evidence: financed via a margin loan or other secured finance arrangement (eg, mortgage, charge or lien (other than a loan from K&S under the K&S Employee Share Plan))

rules.detail: There is no short-term or speculative dealing restriction anywhere in the policy.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or the Deputy Chairman if the Chairman wishes to trade or is uncontactable)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, for onward ASX notification; ASX is also told whether the trade occurred in a Black Out Period requiring prior approval and, if so, whether that approval was obtained
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 3 days (Directors have agreed to notify the Company Secretary within 3 days of dealing)
clearance.evidence: If the Chairman or Deputy Chairman (as the case may be) approves trading in K&S Securities in a Black Out Period, that approval is valid for a period of one week. ... Directors have agreed with K&S to provide notice of such dealings to the Company Secretary of K&S within 3 days after such dealings.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, who informs all other Directors; ASX, only once security interests/third-party rights reach 5% of issued K&S shares, excluding trigger-price detail
clearance.evidence: the Company Secretary must be advised and the Company Secretary will inform all other Directors. The Company Secretary will also disclose to the ASX where the Director, Secretary or Senior Executive holds at least 5% of K&S' issued shares subject to security interests or third party rights.

exceptions.evidence: the Director or Senior Executive is experiencing severe financial hardship which cannot be satisfied or resolved other than by them selling K&S Securities
the Director or Senior Executive is required to sell or transfer K&S Securities in accordance with a court order or undertaking or settlement enforceable by a court, eg, a bona fide family settlement
the sale of K&S Securities as a result of a secured lender to a Director or Senior Executive exercising its rights, eg, under a margin lending arrangement

the transfer of K&S Securities from a holding controlled by the Director or Senior Executive into a self managed superannuation fund in respect of which the Director or Senior Executive is a beneficiary
an investment in, or trading in the units of, a superannuation fund where the assets of the fund are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertaking to accept, or accepting, a takeover offer for K&S

taking up rights under an offer or invitation made to all or most of K&S' shareholders such as a rights issue, share purchase plan, or dividend reinvestment plan, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board of K&S

an Executive Director or Senior Executive is ceasing their employment with K&S and wishes to have K&S Securities acquired by them under the K&S Corporation Limited Employee Share Plan ("ESP") sold by K&S to discharge (in whole or in part) the balance of any loan advanced to the Executive Director or Senior Executive as part of the ESP.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Disclosure to the ASX of a 5%-plus security interest will not extend to specific details such as a trigger price under a margin loan.
financing_disclosure: Directors, Secretary and Senior Executives; trigger: holding financed via a margin loan or other secured finance arrangement; to: Company Secretary, who informs all other Directors; deadline: not specified

Directors, Secretary and Senior Executives; trigger: security interests/third-party rights reach 5% of issued K&S shares; to: ASX (via the Company Secretary), excluding trigger-price detail; deadline: not specified

external_documents: K&S Corporation Limited Employee Share Plan (ESP) rules
exemption_authority: The Chairman or Deputy Chairman may approve trading during a Black Out Period as 'exceptional circumstances' (severe financial hardship, a court-ordered sale/transfer, or an outgoing Executive Director/Senior Executive's ESP loan being discharged via a K&S sale of ESP shares); the request must be made in writing and any approval is valid for one week.

bespoke_clauses.clause: trading in shares of K&S Corporation Limited ("K&S Securities")
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, 'K&S Securities' is defined as shares only, with no reference anywhere to options, derivatives or other financial products, creating a real argument that an OTC, cash-settled put/call over K&S shares is not 'dealing in K&S Securities' at all and so sits entirely outside the policy's Black Out Period and clearance regime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the sale of K&S Securities as a result of a secured lender to a Director or Senior Executive exercising its rights, eg, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale of the collared shares on default is expressly 'excluded trading' permitted even inside a 60-day Black Out Period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: notification not approval for secured financing
bespoke_clauses.clause: the Company Secretary must be advised and the Company Secretary will inform all other Directors.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Financing the holding via a margin loan or other secured arrangement (which would include a collar loan) requires only notification to the Company Secretary, not prior approval, making the loan leg comparatively easy to put in place.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ASX disclosure of Black Out Period approval status
bespoke_clauses.clause: whether the change occurred in a Black Out Period in circumstances where prior written approval of the Chairman or Deputy Chairman (as the case may be) was required; and if prior written approval was required, whether that approval was obtained.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's derivative legs were ever treated as 'dealing' by analogy and executed in a Black Out Period, the market would be told via ASX notification that approval was required and whether it was obtained, adding public visibility to the transaction's timing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (other than a loan from K&S under the K&S Employee Share Plan)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The section 11 notification regime is for third-party secured financing (like a bank collar loan); it does not apply to the Company's own ESP loans, which are a separate, distinguishable financing arrangement.

summary: K&S Corporation's policy defines 'K&S Securities' as shares only, never mentioning options, derivatives, warrants or other financial products, so a cash-settled OTC put/call over K&S shares arguably falls entirely outside the policy's dealing, Black Out Period and clearance provisions on a literal reading. The loan leg is squarely addressed, however: section 11 requires a Director, Company Secretary or Senior Executive financing their holding via 'a margin loan or other secured finance arrangement (eg, mortgage, charge or lien)' to notify the Company Secretary (who informs the other Directors), with ASX disclosure only once security interests reach 5% of issued shares and never extending to trigger-price detail - a notification regime, not an approval gate, so a collar-secured loan should be straightforward to put in place. A secured lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly 'excluded trading' permitted even during the 60-day Black Out Periods before half-year and full-year results. If the derivative legs were nonetheless treated as 'dealing' by analogy, Directors and Senior Executives would need Chairman (or Deputy Chairman) approval to trade in a Black Out Period, valid for one week, with ASX later told whether such approval was required and obtained. Overall a funded collar looks readily achievable, with the main open question being the definitional gap on whether the derivative legs are 'dealing' at all, and the loan leg subject only to notification rather than consent.
